touches.text: Machine: tools plus the glue that holds them together. Has an owner. Lives inside its device (cairn/devices/<device>/machines/<machine>/), or in cairn/machines/ if several devices hold one.

The line between tool and machine is simple vs. complex, and it is measured, not judged. A tool calls no other Cairn component (stdlib and base only) and owns no state of its own. Anything that calls another component, or owns state it must gate, is a machine. A tool that uses other tools is a machine. Tools and machines are peers in the tree; the rung is complexity, not rank. (Q#1, Akien 2026-11-03: "strict")
A device owns its state: only the device writes under its own ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/ tree.
A device holds machines and uses tools (from cairn/tools/). A tool's data for that device lives under the device: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/
A device's own state lives in its ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/ tree.

Research (V1 5.1.1: "delegated learning, research and answering queries"): the librarian goes out on its own, through the general web operator machine (17.14), which it holds as that machine's first user. ("the librarian will get the web interface machine that i don't think exists yet. i believe we built one for you, but we need a general one. i envision a couple of different devices that would use this, the librarian is just the first." Q#28, Akien 2026-11-05)

To come in: the Gmail/Calendar code (today ~/.local/bin/ccgoogle) and CC's browser (~/.local/bin/ccfox), both outside the class now (RULE 1). Their data moves to ~/.cairn/devices/cc/0/tools/<tool>/ (1.2.1).

web_operator: the general machine a device holds to go out on the web. It operates web pages, for reading and other purposes. The web server (18) serves pages; this one works them. (Akien 2026-11-05) NOT BUILT YET. Several devices will hold it; the librarian is the first (9.3.8). The one built for CC (ccfox, ~/.local/bin/ccfox, 12.4.1) is the precedent, not this machine: it is CC's alone. Each holder keeps its own data under ~/.cairn/devices/<holder>/<n>/machines/web_operator/ (1.2.1). (Q#28, Akien 2026-11-05)
